**Reasoning**

The optimal ordering is obtained by sorting the strings of the integers with the comparator  

\[
a\prec b\;\text{iff}\; a\!+\!b > b\!+\!a .
\]

To find the position of 2025 we count how many integers \(n\) satisfy  

\[
n\!+\!2025 > 2025\!+\!n .
\]

---

### 1. Numbers whose first digit > 2  
All numbers beginning with 3–9 precede 2025.  
Count (1‑ to 5‑digit numbers):

\[
\begin{aligned}
&1\text{-digit}: 7 \\
&2\text{-digit}: 7\!\times\!10 = 70 \\
&3\text{-digit}: 7\!\times\!100 = 700 \\
&4\text{-digit}: 7\!\times\!1000 = 7000 \\
&5\text{-digit}: 7\!\times\!10000 = 70000 \\
\hline
&\text{Total}=77777 .
\end{aligned}
\]

### 2. Numbers beginning with **21–29**  
Since the second digit > 0, they also precede 2025.

\[
9\text{ prefixes} \times (1+10+100+1000)=9\!\times\!1111=9999 .
\]

Running total: \(77777+9999=87776\).

### 3. Numbers beginning with **203–209**  
Third digit > 2, so they come before 2025.

\[
7\text{ prefixes} \times (1+10+100)=7\!\times\!111=777 .
\]

Running total: \(87776+777=88553\).

### 4. Numbers **2026–2029**  
Fourth digit > 5, therefore they precede 2025.

\[
4\text{ prefixes} \times (1+10)=4\!\times\!11=44 .
\]

Running total: \(88553+44=88597\).

### 5. Five‑digit numbers **2025x** (x = 2,…,9)  

Compare \(2025x\!+\!2025\) with \(2025\!+\!2025x\).  
The first differing digit is \(x\) versus ‘2’; if \(x>2\) (3–9) the former is larger, and when \(x=2\) the later tie‑break also makes it larger. Thus \(x=2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9\) (8 numbers) are before 2025.  

Running total: \(88597+8=88605\).

---

All other numbers (starting with 1, 20, 200, 201, 2020‑2024, 20250‑20251) are **after** 2025.

Hence the count of integers that appear before 2025 is **88605**, so the index of 2025 is  

\[
i = 88605 + 1 = 88606 .
\]

The proposed solution gave 88607, which is off by one.
